merged.title: feat(port): HDR output on the Vulkan renderer
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** the game always went to the screen in SDR. On a desktop in HDR mode it looked dim and washed out.

**After:** with `hdr = auto` or `on` (Vulkan), the picture goes out as HDR10 or scRGB, with the game's white at the player's paper white, so it looks like SDR. While HDR is on, the frame is drawn in half floats. Each draw's colour is still clamped to 0..1, so only the game's own blending (glows, explosions, lasers) goes above white. That light rolls off towards the display's peak. Off by default, and nothing changes when it is off.

**How:**
- `renderer/hdr.h`: the arithmetic (PQ, BT.2020, roll-off, levels).
- `hdr_encode.comp`: one compute pass into the swapchain image.
- `surface_format.h`: picks the format, falling back to SDR.
- Clamped fragment variant per program (`clamped_fragment`), made only for the HDR frame.
- Settings: Video options, the drawer, the settings file and the launcher (`OPENRAC_HDR`).
- Android: reads the display's HDR/SDR headroom through GameActivity.

merged.title: fix(port): keep white moby glow colours on Vulkan
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody: mesh.vert decoded a moby's glow word (instance w = 1 + RGB) as int(w - 1.0 + 0.5). For a white glow (0xFFFFFF) w is 2^24, and 2^24 - 1 + 0.5 rounds back up to 2^24 in a float, so the colour became 0x1000000: black. Mesa's GL compiler folds the constants and hides it; the Vulkan path does not, so glow packets in white went dark there, like the lit floor under the Giant Clank pad's grate on Quartu and Veldin. Round w first, then take the 1 off.

merged.title: feat(enhanced): pack probe depth as RG16 UNORM
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
Canonical probe depth maps currently use 512 bytes per probe for RG32F moments. Store normalized mean and spread in RG16 UNORM with 16 bytes of FP32 ranges instead, bringing depth storage to 272 bytes per probe, a 46.9% reduction including the ranges.

The encoder uses precision curves for blocker-depth endpoints and small spreads. The shader reconstructs FP32 total variance from two native hardware gathers, preserving octahedral gutters. Colour compression and relocation metadata remain independent. Format 8 invalidates automatic bake caches; legacy version 6 raw moments and version 7 RG8/ASTC depth remain readable.

Reject GPU-packed encoder inputs before plane access and omit unused raw-depth staging. Add CPU codec, malformed-input, parallel encoding and production GPU upload/sampling regressions, and update the native cache integration test. No baked game assets are included.

Validation:
- Windows incremental baker and relevant probe test builds passed. Existing warnings in unchan

merged.title: perf(port): build shaders behind the loading screen on Vulkan and OpenGL
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before.** Vulkan compiled a pipeline the first time a program was drawn in a new state, mid-frame. One pre-warm worker ran and nobody waited for it. The pipeline cache was saved only on a clean exit. OpenGL drivers recompiled programs at the first draw in a new state too.

**After.** Shaders from earlier runs are built during the loading screen on both APIs. A new Vulkan pipeline is linked from parts at once (graphics pipeline library, like DXVK), and the optimised one replaces it later. Nothing drawn changes.

**How.**
- `vk-pipeline-library` (desktop only): shader parts are built at program link; a new pipeline is fast-linked, then swapped for the full one.
- 1 to 4 pre-warm workers; `vkgl::finish_pipelines()` waits for them at level load.
- Pipeline cache and manifest saved in the background at each load and every 2 minutes.
- `gl-state-warmup`: saves each new draw state per driver and draws it once at level load into a private 4x4 target.

**Tested.** Container (lavapipe, llvmpip

merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
Original stencil shadows only accepted Ratchet’s class, so playable Clank did not submit his animated shadow proxies. merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
A cancelled develop job published a partial compiler-cache snapshot which later PRs restored. The slow compatibility run on #217 got only 3.56% compiler-cache hits and spent 31m37s building.

PRs remain restore-only. Prefer successful snapshots, then fall back to older keys so existing caches remain usable. Preserve Windows/POSIX archive path spelling, per-job namespaces and cache-size limits. Restore before configuration so an archived ccache.conf cannot override the current job's settings.

Canonical probe depth maps currently use 512 bytes per probe for RG32F moments. Store normalized mean and spread in RG16 UNORM with 16 bytes of FP32 ranges instead, bringing depth storage to 272 bytes per probe, a 46.9% reduction including the ranges.

opened.author: nickyyOO

**After.** Shaders from earlier runs are built during the loading screen on both APIs. A new Vulkan pipeline is linked from parts at once (graphics pipeline library, like DXVK), and the optimised one replaces it later. Nothing drawn changes.

- `vk-pipeline-library` (desktop only): shader parts are built at program link; a new pipeline is fast-linked, then swapped for the full one.
- 1 to 4 pre-warm workers; `vkgl::finish_pipelines()` waits for them at level load.
- Pipeline cache and manifest saved in the background at each load and every 2 minutes.
- `gl-state-warmup`: saves each new draw state per driver and draws it once at level load into a private 4x4 target.

**Tested.** Container (lavapipe, llvmpip

opened.title: fix(port): Vulkan pipeline parts take only their own state; bindings only their own stages
opened.author: Veradictus
opened.untrustedBody:
#216's pipeline-library linking built each shared part with the whole state of the first key that needed it. NVIDIA (GTX 1070, 580.178) carried the vertex input given to the shared output part into every pipeline linked from it, so draws with another vertex layout read the wrong vertices. llvmpipe ignores the extra state, which is why CI passed.

Six Vulkan tests failed on NVIDIA from #216 on: render_equivalence_vulkan, render_equivalence_vulkan_remaining, enhanced_rendering_vulkan, sun_shadow_vulkan, sun_shadow_filter_reference_vulkan, probe_gpu_vulkan.

- Each part now gets only its own state (vertex input and assembly; viewport and rasteriser; depth and stencil; blend and samples) and null for the rest. Part sharing, fast linking and the prewarm workers are unchanged, so the speed-up stays.
- `vulkan_prewarm` gains a test: one program drawn with two vertex layouts, linked against whole pipelines. It fails on NVIDIA without the fix.
- #216's own linked-parts test now runs with prewar

opened.author: Lynder063
opened.untrustedBody:
The index now takes GitHub's digest as an archive's hash, so SHA256SUMS is optional.
If both exist they must match; with neither, a native release is still skipped.
